title: Tennessee's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Tennessee's 1st Congressional District, covering the Tri-Cities region in northeastern Tennessee, pits incumbent Republican U.S. Representative Diana Harshbarger against three Democratic primary candidates and several independent candidates. The district is heavily Republican and has not elected a Democrat to Congress since the 19th century. Tennessee redrew its congressional map in May 2026, but the 1st District remained largely intact. The primary election is scheduled for August 6, 2026, with the general election on November 3, 2026.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found for this race. The 1st District is considered a Safe/Solid Republican seat by all major election forecasters.

candidates.name: Diana Harshbarger
candidates.summary: Diana Harshbarger is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2020. She is a pharmacist and business owner from Kingsport who serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and is a member of the Freedom Caucus. Harshbarger is seeking re-election to a fourth term.

career_history.title: Pharmacist and Business Owner
career_history.description: Licensed pharmacist since 1987; co-owns a compounding pharmacy with her husband

candidates.name: Kristi Burke
candidates.summary: Kristi Burke is a Democratic candidate for U.S. House in Tennessee's 1st Congressional District. She is a muralist, artist, and community activist from Chuckey, Tennessee who describes herself as a grassroots candidate focused on healthcare, workers' rights, and accountability. Burke is running her first campaign for elected office.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, which necessarily suppresses confidence. However, the structural evidence is exceptionally strong: the district is described as heavily Republican, has not elected a Democrat to Congress since the 19th century, and all major election forecasters rate it a Safe/Solid Republican seat. The May 2026 redistricting left the 1st District largely intact. Incumbent Republican Diana Harshbarger (seeking a fourth term) benefits from incumbency, name recognition, and a district with a deeply entrenched GOP lean. The Democratic primary field consists of three first-time candidates (Kristi Burke, Hernan H. Garcia, David S. Kerr Jr.) who will compete in an August 6 primary against each other, and four independent candidates are also on the general election ballot — none show evidence in the provided data of fundraising or organizational strength sufficient to meaningfully contest the seat. Given the district's partisan composition and historical voting patterns, an overwhelming Republican advantage is virtually certain even though no direct polling corroboration exists.
